newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FORECAST - KNP BT seen posting higher H1 net.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - KNP BT seen posting higher H1 net.

text.p: Dutch paper and office equipment group NV Koninklijke KNP BT is seen posting higher 1997 first-half earnings on Thursday in a turnaround from weak results in previous years, analysts said on Monday.
"We expect the half-year figures will show that KNP BT has left its suffering behind and that it has started an uptrend," analyst Patrick Rutten of bank Van Lanschot said.

Analysts' estimates for KNP BT's 1997 first-half net from ordinary operations ranged from 105 to 142 million guilders ($68.4 million), with the consensus at 127.8 million. Last year, KNP BT posted a first-half net from ordinary activities of 101 million.

The company previously said it would have a one-off gain of about 180 million guilders this year from the sale of one of its packagings units, but a large part of this gain would be used to finance ongoing reorganisations.
Rutten's estimates were at the higher end of the forecast range, with an expected first-half net from ordinary operations of 136.5 million guilders and a second quarter net of 85 million.
Rutten said all KNP BT's divisions now seemed to be on their way up although some were still suffering from difficult market conditions.
The group's paper division had returned to profits but was still plagued by market overcapacity and the packagings division was still being reorganised.
Analyst Jan Wirken at research bureau IRIS was less optimistic with an estimated second-quarter operating net of 61 million guilders, up from 51 million in the year-ago period.
He said KNP BT's paper division had recovered slightly but its market was over-supplied.
"The paper division is still being hit by low prices and KNP BT has no pricing power of its own," Wirken said.
Wirken said KNP BT could not raise prices at the moment as clients had built up large stocks at low price levels.
Added to this, raw material prices have been rising sharply since the start of 1997, putting pressure on margins.

But Rutten said paper demand was expected to pick up, fuelled by good economic prospects in Europe and the United States, and he expected KNP BT would be able to raise its paper prices in September, as the company previously announced.
If this price rise proves to be successful, it could be the start of a spiral of several increases, Rutten said.
Both analysts thought KNP BT was still in talks to find a strategic partner for its paper division Leykam, but did not expect the company to announce a deal soon.

Wirken said he believed KNP BT was negotiating with Sweden's Stora, which he described as a logical partner. Rutten said Finland's Enso was another possibility. Previously, both Scandinavian firms have declined to comment on rumours about teaming up with KNP BT.
But Rutten added that market speculation about KNP BT finding a possible partner had already been discounted in its share price, which today rose to a year-high of 49.00 guilders.
